record.paper_title: Open Problems in Data-Sharing Peer-to-Peer Systems
record.original_question: Is it possible to decouple peer autonomy from robustness in a peer-to-peer search mechanism, so that the system designer can vary autonomy independently while still preserving stable service under node failures and departures?

evidence.quote: Decoupling autonomy from robustness is also important, because it allows greater flexibility in choosing the desired properties of the mechanism.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a peer-to-peer search system modeled as a dynamic network of autonomous nodes that may join, leave, or fail at arbitrary times. Each node independently decides which other nodes to connect to, what queries to forward, and what local resources to share; the degree of "autonomy" of the design is a parameter measuring how freely each node may make these decisions without coordination from a central authority or fixed protocol-imposed constraints. The "robustness" of the system is a parameter measuring the stability of its search service — for example, the probability that queries are answered correctly within a bounded number of hops — under adversarial schedules of node failures and departures.

Question: Does there exist a peer-to-peer search mechanism, together with a formal model of the above kind, in which the autonomy parameter and the robustness parameter can be tuned independently? More precisely, is it possible to design a search mechanism whose autonomy level can be increased or decreased by the system designer while a chosen robustness guarantee continues to hold, and conversely whose robustness can be strengthened without forcing a reduction in node autonomy?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface a definitive resolution. The literature on P2P search continues to discuss tradeoffs among autonomy, robustness, and efficiency, with various mechanisms aiming to preserve local autonomy while improving resilience, but no result establishes a clean independent decoupling of the two as a general design principle.

status_evidence.title: Survey of research towards robust peer-to-peer networks: Search methods
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys research on robust P2P search methods, treating robustness and autonomy as coupled design concerns.
status_evidence.claim: The interaction of autonomy and robustness remains an active design issue rather than a settled question.

status_evidence.title: An efficient resource discovery framework for pure unstructured peer-to-peer systems
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a framework preserving local autonomy while improving search success rates.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works pursue mechanisms that maintain autonomy alongside robustness, but do not claim formal independence of the two parameters.
